Summary

On May 22-23, 1948, the Alexandroni Brigade of the Haganah (which became the IDF) attacked the Palestinian coastal village of Tantura. The village had a population of approximately 1,500 and was known for its fishing industry. Despite attempts at surrender and raising white flags, Israeli forces conducted house-to-house searches, separated men from women and children, and executed male villagers.

An estimated 200-250 Palestinian men were systematically executed after the village surrendered. Bodies were buried in multiple mass graves, including one beneath what is now the parking lot of Dor Beach. The massacre remained largely unknown until 1998 when Israeli graduate student Teddy Katz documented it through interviews with both Palestinian survivors and Israeli soldiers who participated.

Despite initial confirmation by veterans, Katz faced a libel lawsuit and was forced under pressure to sign an 'apology' (later withdrawn). Israeli authorities have consistently refused to excavate the mass graves or conduct official investigations. No perpetrators were prosecuted. The village was demolished and Kibbutz Nahsholim was built on its ruins.

Timeline

May 22, Early Morning
Attack begins
Alexandroni Brigade attacks Tantura from land and sea. Village largely defenseless with minimal weapons.
Katz research; Israeli soldier testimonies
May 22, Morning
Village surrenders
Village elders raise white flags and negotiate surrender. Villagers told they will be safe if they comply. Israeli soldier: 'There was no battle. They raised white flags.'
Israeli soldier testimony (Katz interviews)
May 22, Late Morning
Separation of men from families
Men separated from women and children. Males aged 15-60 gathered in village square and on the beach.
Survivor testimonies; soldier accounts
May 22-23, Day and Night
Mass executions
Systematic execution of male prisoners throughout day and night. Groups taken to execution sites (cemetery, beach, village well) and shot. Soldier: 'They lined them up and shot them... I participated in the whole thing.'
Israeli soldier testimonies (Katz research; 2022 documentary)
May 23, Morning
Mass burial
Bodies buried in mass graves at various locations including beach and cemetery. Some survivors forced to dig graves. Soldier: 'We were ordered to bury them. Some Arab women were forced to help dig.'
Soldier testimonies; survivor accounts
May 23-24
Expulsion of survivors
Surviving women, children, elderly expelled from village. Many sent to Furaydis. Village looted; property confiscated.
Survivor testimonies; Zochrot documentation
1948-1950
Village demolished; cover-up begins
Tantura demolished. Kibbutz Nahsholim established on village ruins (1948-1950). Mass graves concealed; massacre suppressed from Israeli history.
Zochrot; historical records
1998-2000
The Katz Affair
Teddy Katz documents massacre through 140+ interviews with veterans and survivors. Alexandroni veterans sue for libel despite their own testimonies. Katz forced to sign 'apology' under pressure (later withdrawn); thesis downgraded.
Court documents; Haaretz reporting
2022
Documentary renews attention
'Tantura' film by Alon Schwarz features recorded soldier testimonies confirming massacre. Released at Sundance; Israeli authorities continue to refuse excavation of mass graves.
Al Jazeera; documentary coverage

Testimony

Anonymous Alexandroni Brigade Soldier
“There was no battle. They raised white flags... We gathered the men and took them. Some were taken to the cemetery, others to the beach. They lined them up and shot them. I participated in the whole thing.”
Interview with Teddy Katz (1998)
Mariam Al-Yahya
“They separated the men from us. We heard shooting all day and into the night. In the morning, we were told to leave. We never saw our men again. My father, my two brothers, my uncle - all gone.”
Survivor testimony documented by Teddy Katz (1998)
Binyamin Shechter
“I know of three locations where people were killed and buried: the cemetery, the beach south of the village, and near the village well. The numbers? I estimate about 200-230 people were killed.”
Interview in 'Tantura' documentary (2022)
Haim Hermesh
“They took them in groups, men aged 15 and up. They were shot. I saw the bodies. After some time, we were ordered to bury them. Some of the Arab women were forced to help dig.”
Testimony recorded by Teddy Katz, later confirmed in court documents
Fawziyya Saleh
“They made us carry bodies. I saw my teacher, dead. I saw men I knew since childhood, all dead on the beach. The soldiers were laughing and smoking cigarettes.”
Oral history interview, Institute for Palestine Studies

War crimes

Mass Execution of Prisoners of War
After village surrendered, male prisoners systematically executed. Israeli soldier: 'They lined them up and shot them... I participated in the whole thing.' Violations of laws of war regarding treatment of POWs.
📄 Haaretz Investigation 2022 ↗
Execution After Surrender
Village raised white flags and negotiated surrender. Promises of safety violated. Soldier: 'There was no battle. They raised white flags... We gathered the men and took them.'
📄 Soldier Testimonies ↗
Executions on the Beach
Multiple testimonies describe executions on Tantura beach. Survivor: 'They took the men in groups... we heard shooting. They didn't come back.' Bodies left on beach before burial.
📄 IPS Oral History ↗
Mass Graves and Concealment of Evidence
Bodies buried in multiple mass graves at cemetery, beach, and village well. One grave beneath current Dor Beach parking lot. Intelligence officer: 'I know of three locations... I estimate about 200-230 people were killed.' Israeli authorities refuse excavation.
📄 Documentary Evidence ↗
Separation of Families
Deliberate separation of men from women and children before executions. Women and children forced to witness aftermath; some forced to bury bodies.
Looting and Complete Destruction
Systematic looting of homes, theft of valuables, fishing boats, property. Village completely demolished. Kibbutz Nahsholim established on village lands; mass grave covered by parking lot.
📄 Zochrot Documentation ↗
Forced Expulsion
Surviving population forcibly expelled to nearby villages. Prevented from returning or burying their dead. Property confiscated under Israeli Absentee Property Law.

Legal classification

Law Applicable in May 1948
Hague Convention IV (1907): Customary by 1948. Art. 23(c): killing enemies who laid down arms; Art. 23(d): 'no quarter' declarations; Art. 25: attack on undefended places; Art. 28: pillage; Art. 46: protection of family honor, lives, property.
Post-1949 Context (Descriptive Classification)
Geneva Convention IV (1949): Adopted Aug 12, 1949 (3 months after Tantura). Israel ratified Jul 6, 1951. Art. 3: Prohibition of violence to life and person, including murder of persons taking no active part in hostilities. Not applicable retroactively to May 1948.
Treaty Opposability
Vienna Convention principle: Treaties not retroactive (Art. 28). Geneva IV cannot be invoked for events predating its adoption.
Law Applicable in May 1948
Martens Clause (1899/1907): Humanitarian principles binding even where not explicitly codified.
Post-1949 Context (Descriptive Classification)
Rome Statute (1998): Modern framework characterizing acts as crimes against humanity (murder, persecution, deportation) and war crimes (willful killing of POWs, attacking civilians who surrendered). Used descriptively; not retroactive enforcement.
Treaty Opposability
Customary IHL: Hague 1907 + Martens Clause bound all parties in 1948 regardless of ratification.
Law Applicable in May 1948
Note: These instruments were opposable to all parties in 1948 as customary international humanitarian law.
Post-1949 Context (Descriptive Classification)
Note: Modern classifications aid understanding but do not create retroactive legal obligations.

Commanders

Dan Epstein
Overall brigade command during coastal operations; responsible for Tantura assault planning and execution. Continued military career in IDF; honored as brigade founder. Never prosecuted; never publicly acknowledged massacre despite subordinate testimonies
Katz, Teddy. MA Thesis (1998) - Based on IDF archives and veteran interviews
Binyamin Shechter
Present during operations; witnessed executions and burials. Testified: 'I know of three locations where people were killed and buried... I estimate about 200-230 people were killed.'. Civilian life; broke silence in interviews with Katz (1998) and documentary (2022). Never prosecuted despite admitting direct knowledge; testimonies recorded but ignored by Israeli authorities
Schwarz, Alon. 'Tantura' documentary (2022) - On-camera testimony
Haim Hermesh
Participated in operations; testified: 'They took them in groups, men aged 15 and up. They were shot... we were ordered to bury them.'. Civilian life; provided testimony to Katz confirming executions and burials. Never prosecuted despite confession of participation in killings and burials
Katz, Teddy. MA Thesis (1998) - Interview testimony
Anonymous Alexandroni Veterans (Multiple)
Over 135 veterans interviewed by Katz; many confirmed executions, mass graves, and systematic killings. Several provided detailed locations and casualty estimates.. Various civilian careers; some became prominent in Israeli society. None prosecuted; many initially confirmed accounts then sued Katz for libel despite their own recorded testimonies
Katz, Teddy. Research archive - 140+ interviews (1998)
Teddy Katz (Researcher)
Not a perpetrator; included here for his role in uncovering suppressed history through 140+ interviews. Academic career destroyed after Alexandroni veterans' libel suit; forced under pressure to sign 'apology' (later withdrawn); suffered psychological breakdown. Victim of suppression campaign; his research validated by 2022 documentary but never officially acknowledged
Haaretz. 'The Tantura Massacre and the Man Who Revealed It' (2022)
